River’s 2025 Report: 1.57M BTC Lost in Self-Custody vs. 1.51M BTC on Exchanges  Source: https://river.com/learn/files/river-custody-report-2025.pdf

tweet.text:
It is statistically safer to store coins on exchanges than to self custody. 👇

A few thoughts:

Assuming the data is correct, my impression is Willy has always been a strong supporter for self custody.

Hack data is easier to collect on the CEX side, usually major news. It is harder on the self-custody side, where hacks, lost coins, etc are often not reported.

On the exchange side, some deceased exchanges drag down the data. Binance (and a few other exchanges) have always covered users for any CEX side hacks.

Not saying one is better than another. Different approaches have different risk profiles (and product offerings), and may be better suited for different people. A balanced approach is probably best.

FWA holders upset that none of the substantial protocol fees generated during Fake World Assets’ initial two-week launch period were directed to token buybacks and instead went to TokenWorks.
Just last week this was shilled as Christ’s second coming
Source

tweet.text:
These sections of the docs have not changed since a week before launch. 

Yes, TokenWorks makes money. I'm personally of the belief that if you build an innovative product you should be rewarded, just as traders do. The goal is move future incoming fees (starting tomorrow) from going to TokenWorks to the token and make a sustainable protocol. 

There is no percentage of retroactive fees that would satisfy everyone. If you were hoping a large portion fees would be used for this I’m sorry, but it was never stated or even hinted at. I also don’t think it would do anything other than temporarily increase the token price, only for people to sell into it. 

I'd rather use it to keep building the protocol and add new features just like we've been planning from the start.

That being said, I do hear the feedback and I know everyone is just speaking from a place of wanting to see the protocol succeed. and for the protocol to succeed, more of the future fees need to stay within the ecosystem.
